policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: The variant is an adverbial/ascensive kai before diakonon. ASV 'who is a servant of the church' has no 'also', but ASV routinely leaves such kai untranslated, so the English neither requires nor excludes it. The only note here is classed alternative_rendering ('Or, deaconess') and concerns English wording for diakonon, not the presence of kai.
Pure word order (pronoun before or after the verb). ASV 'that ye receive her in the Lord' renders the same words in normal English order and cannot register Greek sequence. No note is mapped here.
Pure word order within the emphatic pronoun phrase. ASV 'and of mine own self' renders both words identically under either sequence. No note is mapped here.
ASV reads 'the first-fruits of Asia unto Christ'. 'Asia' renders Asias; the alternative Achaias would have produced 'Achaia'. The ASV wording distinguishes the reading.
Mariam and Marian are the Semitic and Hellenised accusative forms of the same name; both are rendered 'Mary'. ASV 'Salute Mary' cannot distinguish them and no note is mapped here.
ASV reads 'who bestowed much labor on you'. 'You' renders humas; the alternative hemas would have given 'on us'. The ASV wording distinguishes the reading.

The two candidates differ only in accent, and the accent fixes the name's gender: Iounian is the feminine Junia, Iounian (perispomenon) the masculine Junias. ASV's text reads 'Junias', which renders the masculine form; the margin 'Or, Junia' is classed alternative_rendering and only records the other transliteration, so the printed text is what decides.

gegonan and gegonasin are alternative third-plural perfect endings of the same verb with the same sense. ASV 'who also have been in Christ before me' renders either identically. The mapped note is alternative_rendering about the name Junia and does not touch this unit.
ASV reads 'Salute Ampliatus my beloved in the Lord'. 'Ampliatus' transliterates Ampliaton; the alternative Amplian would have produced 'Amplias'. The ASV wording distinguishes the reading.
sungene and sungenen are orthographic variants of the same accusative singular. ASV 'Herodion my kinsman' renders either identically; no note is mapped here.

ASV reads 'Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas' in that order, which excludes r02 (RP), where Hermas stands first and Hermes last. The remaining two candidates differ only in the printed punctuation between the names, which English cannot register, so the base fallback carries the projection.
ASV reads 'All the churches of Christ salute you'. 'All' renders pasai, which the alternative omits. The ASV wording distinguishes the reading.

The variant is present versus aorist imperative of the same verb; ASV 'and turn away from them' renders either without marking aspect. The mapped note is alternative_rendering ('Or, teaching') for didache and does not touch this unit.
ASV reads 'serve not our Lord Christ', with no 'Jesus'. The alternative adds Iesou, which the ASV wording does not render.

The candidates differ in word order and in RP's articular to eph' humin; ASV 'I rejoice therefore over you' renders the same elements in ordinary English order and does not reflect the Greek sequence or the article. No note is mapped here.

The variant adds the particle men correlating with the following de. ASV 'wise unto that which is good, and simple unto that which is evil' leaves men untranslated as usual, so the English neither requires nor excludes it.
ASV reads 'The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you'. 'Christ' renders Christou, which the alternative omits. The ASV wording distinguishes the reading.

ASV reads 'Timothy my fellow-worker saluteth you; and Lucius and Jason and Sosipater, my kinsmen' — a singular verb with Timothy alone as its subject, rendering the singular Aspazetai. The plural Aspazontai would have required 'salute' over all the names. The ASV wording distinguishes the reading.

Pure word order of holes within the phrase; ASV 'and of the whole church' renders either sequence identically. The textual_variant note printed at this verse concerns the presence of verse 24 and the grace at verse 20, not the position of holes, so it does not decide this unit.

ASV prints no verse 24 at all; the grace stands instead at verse 20, and the mapped textual_variant note at 16:23 says only that 'some ancient authorities insert here verse 24 ... and omit the like words in verse 20'. The ASV text therefore renders the omission.

ASV has no verse 24, so there is no 'Amen' in the text for the base reading to answer to; the mapped textual_variant note at 16:23 places verse 24 only in 'some ancient authorities'. With r00 excluded by the empty verse, the alternative — which carries the closing doxology — is what the ASV text supports.
